Trail guide · FAQ

How to build a great crawl or trail

A good crawl or trail is one a real person can finish, hungry the whole way.

Crawl, trail or road trip: what's the difference?
CrawlOne food, one area, on foot or a short hop. The same thing at every stop (wings, pizza, hot dogs, sponge candy) in a neighborhood, downtown or one city. Walkable or a few minutes' drive between stops. A few hours, usually one afternoon or evening, with 3 to 6 stops. The point is to compare: who does it best? Order small so the votes are fair. Built for a group.Example: the Buffalo Wing Crawl
TrailA themed route across a region, usually by car. Linked by a theme rather than one exact dish (cider and doughnuts, factory tours, wine, the hot dogs of New York) across a county, a region or several regions. Half a day to a full day, sometimes a weekend or a season-long passport, with 4 to 12 stops. The point is to explore and collect: stamp the passport and finish it.Example: the Cider Doughnut Trail
Road tripThe long haul. Multi-day and multi-region. A road trip can string together crawls and trails along the way.Example: Thruway Eats

Quick test: same food at every stop, close enough to walk or hop between? It's a crawl. A theme you drive to explore? It's a trail. More than a day across regions? It's a road trip.

What kinds of crawls and trails can I build?
A few hours2 to 4 stops, about 4 hours or less. Lunch-to-dinner in one town or neighborhood.
One-day excursion3 to 6 stops in a single day. A morning-to-evening drive with breaks between bites.
Top spots3 to 8 of the best-known places for one food in one area. The "if you only go once" list.
Make your ownYour own theme and pace, 2 to 8 stops. Still has to be finishable in a day.
Local organizer trailFor chambers, BIDs, tourism boards, clubs and food tour companies. Gets a "Local organizer" tag once we verify you.
Should my trail be walkable or drivable?

Pick one and build for it. Walkable trails keep each leg under about 1.5 miles, so the whole thing works on foot in a downtown or village. Drivable trails can cover more ground, but keep each drive reasonable, ideally under an hour between stops. The builder estimates miles and time as you add stops and warns you when a leg is too long for the way you're getting around.

How long should a trail take?

A few-hours trail should fit in about 4 hours. A one-day excursion should fit between breakfast and dinner, about 10 hours including drive time. We count roughly 40 minutes at each stop plus travel. If the builder says your trail runs long, cut a stop or split it into two trails.

Is my crawl, trail or event seasonal?

If it only runs part of the year, mark the months when you build or post it. An apple tour isn't happening in January, and most ice cream stands close after summer. In season, it gets an "In season" badge and shows up in the highlights: Top trails, the Trails menu and the home page. Off-season, it stays listed with "back in [month]" and moves to the end of lists, so nobody drives out to a closed stand. Spot something that looks seasonal but isn't marked? Tap Seasonal? Suggest months on its page. The editor confirms before anything changes.

How many stops is too many?

It's hard to eat 50 chicken wings, so keep it reasonable. Plan for about 3 or 4 food stops in a few hours and no more than 6 in a day. Mix in something light or sweet between heavy stops, and tell people what to order in a small size: "split a dozen," "one slice, not a pie," "a half order of riggies."

There's already an apple trail near me. Can I build another?

Yes. New York has room for a lot of apple trails in the fall. Every crawl, trail and road trip is filed by theme and region, and each theme has its own page (like Apples & cider) that groups them by region, with the most-voted one in each region as its People's pick. When you build, we check for near-copies: if yours has the same theme and region and shares most of the same stops as one already up, we'll suggest voting for it or remixing it instead. Sharing a stop or two is fine. Give yours its own angle: a different stretch of the region, a walkable version, a cider-only route.

How do I build one?
  1. Join the site (free).
  2. In Trails, choose Create a trail.
  3. Name it, choose crawl or trail, pick a theme, the length and walkable or drivable.
  4. Add stops in order. Places already on the site fill in their town for you.
  5. Check the trail estimate, then publish it to share with other seekers, or keep it as a private draft.
How does voting work?

Members vote on every trail: official trails, road trips and member trails. Tap ▲ on any trail you'd recommend. The most-voted trails rise to the top of the Top trails list and get featured. You can't vote on your own trail, and building trails people love earns you Miles toward Trail Blazer status.

What makes a trail great?

One clear theme. Stops in an order that makes sense on a map. A note on what to order at each stop. Check hours and closed days before you publish, especially for seasonal stands, and mention parking if it's tricky. If a stop closes, anyone can report it, and you'll get a heads-up to swap it out.
